verdict.rationale: Honeycomb documents a first-party Kubernetes agent that collects logs and resource metrics from nodes, pods, containers, and volumes, which covers the container and Kubernetes parts of the story. That documentation sits under a "recommended-migrations/migrate-from-honeycomb-kubernetes-agent" path, which suggests the agent is being retired. The remaining ingestion evidence describes application instrumentation via the open-source OpenTelemetry SDKs and OTLP, not vendor-maintained host or cloud integrations. missing for 10: host-level agent coverage, cloud-service integrations (e.g. AWS/GCP/Azure), evidence the Kubernetes agent is current rather than deprecated, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an SRE, I can instrument hosts, containers, Kubernetes, and cloud services through vendor-maintained agents and integrations

citations.quote: Honeycomb integrates with Kubernetes to collect your applications' logs, cluster logs, and resource metrics so that you can answer all the questions you have.
The Honeycomb Kubernetes agent can also collect resource and status metrics from nodes, pods, containers, and volumes.
